description: Read one cited company profile. Its one argument, `domain`, takes the company's domain (`acme.com`) or its exact company name (`Acme Robotics`); there is no separate name argument. The profile gives name, description, HQ, founded year, industry, employee band, social links, a funding rollup (the amount raised across the rounds we hold, not lifetime total raised) and a careers link, with a source URL on every field and each marked `stated` (a page states it) or `inferred` (classified from a page); a field no source supports is null, never guessed. Costs $0.02 per company returned, drawn from your balance. A domain not built yet returns 202 `building` (retry in about 30 seconds), and a domain that does not resolve to a company returns 404; both are free. A build still unfinished after 15 minutes ends in a free 404 `BUILD_TIMED_OUT` (retry in an hour), and a company we hold no publishable profile for is a free 404 `NO_PUBLISHABLE_PROFILE`; stop polling on either. A company name is matched whole against the funding rounds we hold: several companies with that name answer HTTP 300 with each `{name, domain}` to choose from (free, never a guess), and no company with that name is a free 404. The funding rollup counts only rounds in our funding coverage. Coverage: funding rounds are complete from 2026-10-01, partial from 2026-09-22 to 2026-09-30, and only a few earlier rounds are held, so a company whose last round was before that returns none (an empty answer carries a `coverage` object saying so). While GET /pricing does not list this route in its family's available_routes it answers 503 temporarily_unavailable and nothing is charged.

domain.description: The company's domain, for example `acme.com`, or its exact name, for example `Acme Robotics`.
